rules.text: Agent states the call is being recorded near the start of the call.
Agent gives their name, says they are a licensed insurance agent, and names the agency.
No promise of "guaranteed approval" unless the product really is guaranteed issue, and no claim that coverage starts before the carrier approves it.
Agent never says or implies the policy is a government, Medicare, Social Security or state benefit program.
Health questions are read as written. Agent does not coach answers, skip questions or suggest leaving conditions out.
Client gives clear verbal authorization for the bank draft, with premium amount and draft date read back.
The person consenting is the proposed insured or owner. No one else answers or authorizes on their behalf.
Agent asks whether this policy replaces or changes any existing life insurance or annuity, and follows replacement steps if yes.
Coverage amount, monthly premium, policy type, and any waiting or graded period are stated clearly before the client agrees.
No pressure tactics: no false deadlines ("rates go up tomorrow"), no talking over a client who wants to think about it or end the call.
Full SSN and full bank or card numbers are not read back aloud.
Agent mentions the free-look period or the right to cancel.

instructions: Flag anything that seems off even if no rule covers it: a third party in the background prompting the client, a client who sounds confused about what they bought, an agent rushing through disclosures, or statements about price or coverage that contradict each other.
